passages.title: A Visit to a Maya Pyramid
passages.text: Last summer my family travelled to Central America to (1)____ the ruins of an old Maya city. Our guide told us that the Maya had (3)____ it hundreds of years ago without any metal tools. I found that very hard to (4)____. From the top, we could see green forest stretching in every (5)____. The guide explained that the Maya were great watchers of the (6)____, and that their calendar was extremely (7)____. Walking among the silent stones, I began to (8)____ why so many people are drawn to this place. It felt as if the city still kept many (9)____ that no one had solved. That trip made me want to (10)____ more about ancient civilisations.

passages.title: Reading the Maya Calendar
passages.text: The Maya are famous for their amazing (1)____, which could measure the year with great accuracy. To build it, they spent many nights (2)____ the movements of the stars and planets. Slowly, modern scholars have (7)____ many of the signs, though some parts are still not clear. Each new discovery helps us (8)____ how clever this ancient people really were. It is (9)____ that they reached such knowledge without any modern machines. Studying the Maya makes me (10)____ how much skill lies hidden in the past.

passages.title: A Diver's First Deep Dive
passages.text: Tom had trained for months for his first (1)____ into the deep sea. Sitting inside the small underwater (2)____, he watched the sunlight slowly disappear as he sank. Through the window he saw strange (5)____ that glowed in the darkness, creatures he had only seen in books. The (6)____ outside was so great that it could crush an ordinary boat. Tom carefully recorded (7)____ he saw, knowing the data would be useful to scientists. He realised how (8)____ of the ocean people had really explored. When at last he rose back towards the (9)____, he felt proud and amazed. That dive made him want to (10)____ into the secrets of the deep for the rest of his life.
